title: WorkPulse realtime board v1
description: WebSocket projection protocol for the Realtime Command Center board: the server→client `snapshot` and `presence.upsert` frames (no client→server frames in v1). This is a projection of already-recorded attendance and approved-leave facts, not a domain fact — it is not part of the event catalog and carries no envelope (`.ai/features/realtime-command-center.md`). Identifiers and state only — no names, emails, notes or any PII (`.ai/security.md`). Validate a WS message against the root — a union discriminated on `type`; validate a REST `GET /api/v1/realtime/board` body against `#/$defs/board-snapshot`, which is exactly the `snapshot` frame's body.

counts.title: RealtimeBoardCounts
counts.description: Overlapping counts, not a partition (ADR 0009): `late` co-occurs with `present`/`remote`/`checked_out`. Full counts ride every frame — clients never derive them. Clock-driven transitions (absent onset at shift start + grace) push nothing and land on the next ~60s snapshot refresh.

present.description: Employees with an open record for the workday, working onsite.

remote.description: Employees with an open record for the workday, working remote.

late.description: Rows with the orthogonal `late` flag set — a cut across the other statuses, never a status of its own (ADR 0009).

on_leave.description: In-scope employees with APPROVED leave covering the workday. `on_leave` wins over a same-day attendance record (ADR 0014): covered employees are excluded from present/remote/late/checked_out and from absent.

absent.description: In-scope active employees with an expected shift (location's, else tenant default), no record at all for the workday, and now > shift start + grace (ADR 0009; rest-day over-count accepted and documented in UI copy).

checked_out.description: Employees whose attendance record for the workday is closed.

presence-row.title: PresenceRow
presence-row.description: One employee's presence for the current workday: one status plus an orthogonal `late` flag (ADR 0009). Every push is a full-row idempotent upsert — redelivery is harmless and clients never patch partial state.

employee_id.description: Employee the row belongs to (UUIDv7 string). Display names are joined client-side from employee data the web already holds.

status.description: Presence status. `late` is never a status — it is the orthogonal flag below (ADR 0009).

late.description: Set once at check-in against the exclusive shift.start + grace boundary; never cleared.

minutes_late.description: Whole minutes past shift start + grace while `late` is true — recomputed from the record's shift at read/publish time; `null` when not late.

since.description: `checked_in_at` for present/remote, `checked_out_at` for checked_out, `null` for absent/on_leave (UTC ISO 8601).

attendance_id.description: The workday's attendance record (UUIDv7 string); `null` for absent/on_leave rows.

activity-entry.title: RealtimeActivityEntry
activity-entry.description: One recent attendance transition for the activity rail. Identifiers only — the web joins display names.

employee_id.description: Employee the transition belongs to (UUIDv7 string).

action.description: The attendance transition. Lateness rides the check-in row — there is no separate late entry.

board-snapshot.title: RealtimeBoardSnapshot
board-snapshot.description: The one board payload: REST `200` of `GET /api/v1/realtime/board` and the body of the `snapshot` frame (which adds `type`) — one resource, two transports. Current workday only; no date parameter exists anywhere. Rows are unordered (the client sorts); `presence` is uncapped, `activity` is newest-first capped 20.

date.description: Current workday (YYYY-MM-DD, the server UTC date). A delta whose `date` differs from the client's snapshot date makes the client refetch this snapshot instead of patching.

presence.description: Every in-scope employee with a record for the workday, plus every in-scope employee with approved leave covering the workday and every in-scope employee currently counted absent. Uncapped, unordered.

activity.description: Recent attendance transitions, newest first, capped 20.

snapshot-frame.title: RealtimeSnapshotFrame
snapshot-frame.description: First frame after the handshake, and again after every reconnect resync: the whole board as of connect time. Body fields are exactly `#/$defs/board-snapshot` (spelled out here because `additionalProperties: false` cannot compose across `$ref`).

date.description: Current workday (YYYY-MM-DD, the server UTC date).

presence.description: Every in-scope employee with a record for the workday, plus every in-scope employee with approved leave covering the workday and every in-scope employee currently counted absent. Uncapped, unordered.

activity.description: Recent attendance transitions, newest first, capped 20.

presence-upsert-frame.title: RealtimePresenceUpsertFrame
presence-upsert-frame.description: One presence transition projected to every in-scope viewer: the changed row as a full-row idempotent upsert, plus fresh full counts over the connection's known rows — never client-side derivation. Sources are an attendance check-in/check-out or an APPROVED leave covering the consume date (ADR 0014). Transient, at-most-once delivery: missed deltas are recovered by resyncing a snapshot on reconnect (durable replay is Phase 3's outbox + Kafka, feeding this same protocol).

date.description: Workday the delta belongs to (YYYY-MM-DD). If it differs from the client's snapshot date, the client refetches instead of patching.

occurred_at.description: When the transition happened (UTC ISO 8601) — drives the activity rail.

reason.description: Which transition caused the upsert. `leave_approved` carries an on_leave row (no attendance_id/since, late=false) and fires only when the approved range covers the consume date (ADR 0014). A check-out arriving after such an approval keeps the on_leave row (presence is canonical) while still recording the transition in the activity rail. At most one delta per transition; lateness is carried on the row, never as its own frame.
